question:
(a) Explain why electric current in a metal is related to drift velocity, not random thermal velocity.
(b) If the current through a wire is doubled while $n$ and $A$ remain unchanged, how does the drift velocity change? Justify.

options.A:
(a) Random thermal velocity produces current because all electrons move in the same direction on average.
(b) If current is doubled, drift velocity becomes half.
options.B:
(a) Random thermal velocities cancel on average and produce no net charge flow; only drift velocity due to an electric field produces current.
(b) Since $I=neAv_d$, with $n$ and $A$ unchanged, doubling current doubles $v_d$.
options.C:
(a) Current is determined only by thermal velocity, not by drift velocity.
(b) Doubling current leaves drift velocity unchanged.
options.D:
(a) Drift velocity and random thermal velocity are identical.
(b) Doubling current makes $v_d$ four times.
